title: eval-harness: add prompt-set quality gating and CI metrics integration
author: Alyssa Chen
body:
Summary:
Add an opinionated quality-gating layer to the eval-harness that runs prompt-set regressions as part of CI, plus integration of eval metrics into the CI status checks. This enables automated blocking on regressions for tracked prompt-sets and surfaces meaningful metric deltas in PR feedback.

Motivation:
- We frequently see subtle regressions from model rollouts and quantization changes that only appear for specific prompt-sets.
- Manual triage is slow; teams need a deterministic gate and metric visibility in CI to catch regressions early.

This change implements:
- A configurable "prompt quality gate" that runs selected prompt-sets in PRs and compares metric deltas to thresholds.
- Integration with our CI to report a PASS/FAIL with a short metrics summary in the PR checks.
- A lightweight summary artifact (CSV/JSON) uploaded as a build artifact for debugging.
- Docs and examples for adding new prompt-sets and configuring thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] New gating logic and metric comparator (eval_harness/gating.py)
- [x] CI workflow changes to run gated evals (.github/workflows/eval-harness.yml)
- [x] Upload artifacts and a human-readable summary (ci/artifacts.py)
- [x] Docs for configuring gates (docs/eval-harness/quality-gates.md)
- [x] Unit tests and small integration fixture (tests/eval_harness/test_gating.py)
- [x] Back-compat: default gates are opt-in for non-critical repos

Related:
- Linear: ENG-3245 (prompt regression automation)
- Support ticket SUP-1182 (customer reported regression during quantized rollout)

Notes on design decisions:
- Gating runs are limited by default to a small set of canonical prompt-sets to keep CI latency reasonable (~5-7 minutes on our runners). Teams can opt into wider coverage via the repo-level config.
- Thresholds are conservative and configurable; the comparator supports absolute/relative deltas and a trimmed-mean for noisy metrics.
- We intentionally emit a short metrics table in the CI check (precision to 2 decimals) and attach a full artifact for investigation.

How to review:
- Focus on the gating comparator semantics in eval_harness/gating.py and the test fixtures in tests/eval_harness/.
- CI workflow and secrets usage are isolated to the eval-harness job.
- Docs contain a short example for adding a new prompt-set with a suggested threshold.

Manual test summary:
- Ran gating locally against a small model and verified PASS/FAIL semantics with a synthetic regression.
- Exercised artifact upload in a dry-run of the GitHub Actions workflow.

Merge strategy:
- Squash merge into main after approvals and green CI.
commits: Add CI workflow and artifact upload (.github/workflows/eval-harness.yml, ci/artifacts.py)
Docs: quality gates and prompt-set examples (docs/eval-harness/quality-gates.md)
Fix: address flake8 and type hints reported by CI
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Can we make the default gate set smaller for hosted repos? CI latency is currently ~6m in our runner pool.
Alyssa Chen (author): Yes - default is now the 'canonical' small set; added opt-in config for larger sets (see docs).
Priya Natarajan: A few nit comments on naming in comparator and the trimmed-mean implementation; also add a unit test that reproduces an off-by-one in sample count.
Alyssa Chen (author): Addressed nits and added the unit that mimics the earlier off-by-one; pushed fix. CI rerun pending.
Marcus Lee: Approving pending CI - please squash the minor test debug prints.
CI Bot: Initial run failed (flake8 errors). Rerun succeeded after fixes.
release_notes: Add opt-in prompt-set quality gating and CI integration for eval-harness. Teams can configure prompt-sets and thresholds; CI will block on regressions for tracked prompts.
notes: This is an opt-in gate for most repos; platform and infra teams should enable by adding a .eval-gate.yml with the desired prompt-set and thresholds.
